resources.string: Recognises swipes from the screen edges and performs Back, Home and Recents. Used for navigation only: AnyGest never reads screen content, text or keystrokes, and sends nothing off your device.

resources.string: Henrique Almeida (h3nc4) — creator of HyperGesture, the project AnyGest is based on
Created the app: the gestures, the edge touch capture, app switching and the whole foundation AnyGest is built on.
Showed how to open Circle to Search without root by talking directly to Android\'s assistant service. The technique used here is theirs.
All three projects are free software under the GPL-3.0, and so is AnyGest.
All set: your gestures are working.
Gestures are not working yet. Follow the steps in order.
Gestures work. A few steps are left to check.

In App info, open the Advanced settings section and turn on Allow restricted settings. Without it Android will not let AnyGest use Accessibility. The option only appears until it has been allowed; if you do not see it, tap I did it.
In Accessibility, tap AnyGest and turn on Use AnyGest.
In App info, open the battery page and choose no restrictions, so HyperOS does not stop your gestures. If this step stays amber after you chose it, tap I did it.
Turn on autostart for AnyGest so your gestures come back on their own after a restart. HyperOS does not let apps check this, so tap I did it once it is on.
Switching apps from the bottom edge needs usage access to know which app came before.
Google as the digital assistant (Circle to Search)
Circle to Search needs the Google app as the default digital assistant app. If it already is, tap I did it.

If HyperOS stops the gesture service while the button bar is hidden, you are left with no Back and no Home, and the only way out would be restarting the phone. The Control Center still opens with a swipe from the top of the screen, and this shortcut shows whether your gestures are running: when they are stopped, one tap on it opens AnyGest\'s Accessibility page so you can turn it back on.
If the button below is missing or does nothing, edit the Control Center and add the AnyGest shortcut by hand.
In Navigation mode, choose gesture navigation to hide the three-button bar and gain screen space. Your gestures work either way. To bring the bar back, choose the buttons on the same screen.
Turn AnyGest on first (First steps): with the service stopped, a hidden bar leaves you with no way to navigate.
